L0: # Model Context Protocol (MCP)
L1: 
L2: Let your AI agents interact with the Stripe API by using our MCP server.
L3: 
L4: Read this page in your terminal: [install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) (v1.43.3+) and run `stripe docs`. [Reference](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs)
L5: ## Start here: Integrate with Stripe using skills and plugins
L6: 
L7: Stripe provides skills and plugins for agents to build faster and more accurately. See [Agent skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md) for more information.
L8: 
L9: **Quickstart**: [Install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) using the installation script for your operating system, then open a new terminal and run `stripe agent setup`.
L10: The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API and search the Stripe knowledge base, including documentation and support articles.
L11: ## Set up Stripe MCP with a plugin  (Recommended)
L12: 
L13: [Agent plugins](https://docs.stripe.com/agents/plugin.md) for Stripe automatically configure the Stripe MCP server, install our [skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md), and make sure they’re up to date. You get our latest capabilities without configuration or maintenance.
L14: 
L15: Install the Stripe CLI using the installation script for your operating system. Script installations enable [automatic updates](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/upgrade) by default.
L16: On macOS or Linux:
L17: 
L18: ```bash
L19: curl -fsSL https://cli.stripe.com/install.sh | sh
L20: export PATH="$HOME/.stripe/bin:$PATH"
L21: ```
L22: 
L23: On Windows, run the following command in PowerShell:
L24: 
L25: ```powershell
L26: irm https://cli.stripe.com/install.ps1 | iex
L27: ```
L28: 
L29: After installation, open a new terminal and install the agent tooling:
L30: 
L31: ```bash
L32: stripe agent setup
L33: ```
L34: 
L35: This command automatically detects which agents you use, and runs the applicable commands.
L36: ## Manually set up Stripe MCP
L37: 
L38: If your MCP client doesn’t support [agent plugins](https://docs.stripe.com/agents/plugin.md) for Stripe, or you prefer to configure the Stripe MCP server and install the skills manually, follow these instructions:
L39: #### Cursor
L40: 
L41: [Install in Cursor](cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=stripe&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC5zdHJpcGUuY29tIn0%3D)
L42: 
L43: Select **Install in Cursor** to open Cursor and add the Stripe MCP server. To configure it manually, add the following configuration to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`.
L44: 
L45: For more information, see [Cursor’s MCP documentation](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp).
L46: 
L47: ```json
L48: {
L49:  "mcpServers": {
L50:    "stripe": {
L51:      "url": "https://mcp.stripe.com"
L52:    }
L53:  }
L54: }
L55: ```
L56: #### Claude Code
L57: 
L58: Run the following command to add the Stripe MCP server to Claude Code:
L59: 
L60: ```bash
L61: claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com/
L62: ```
L63: 
L64: After you add the server, start Claude Code and run the `/mcp` command to authenticate Stripe with OAuth.
L65: To authenticate with an [agent API key](https://docs.stripe.com/keys.md#agent-keys) instead of OAuth, add the server to your project’s `.mcp.json` file and reference an environment variable that holds your agent API key, rather than passing the key on the command line. In this example, `${AGENT_API_KEY}` is a placeholder; replace `AGENT_API_KEY` with the actual name of your environment variable, and set that environment variable in your shell before running Claude Code.
L66: ```json
L67: {
L68:   "mcpServers": {
L69:     "stripe": {
L70:       "type": "http",
L71:       "url": "https://mcp.stripe.com",
L72:       "headers": {
L73:         "Authorization": "Bearer ${AGENT_API_KEY}"
L74:       }
L75:     }
L76:   }
L77: }
L78: ```
L79: 
L80: For more information, see the [Claude Code MCP documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).
L81: #### Claude Desktop
L82: 
L83: You can [install the official Stripe connector in Claude](https://claude.ai/directory/de127013-63f1-43d0-8dd2-b6cb5b4e5d1b) on the web and in Claude Desktop.
L84: 
L85: 1. Select **Connect to Claude** and add the connector to your account or workspace.
L86: 2. Sign in to your Stripe account and grant permissions to Claude using the OAuth window when prompted.
L87: 3. In a conversation, select the plus icon, select **Connectors**, and enable Stripe.
L88: For Team and Enterprise accounts, an owner must add the connector to the workspace before members can connect their Stripe accounts.
L89: #### Codex
L90: 
L91: Run the following command to add the Stripe MCP server to Codex:
L92: 
L93: ```bash
L94: codex mcp add stripe --url https://mcp.stripe.com
L95: ```
L96: 
L97: The ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI, and Codex IDE extension support MCP servers and share the same configuration on your computer. To learn more, see the OpenAI [Codex MCP documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp).
L98: After you authenticate, you can switch between the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI, and Codex IDE extension without configuring the Stripe MCP server again.
L99: To authenticate with an [agent API key](https://docs.stripe.com/keys.md#agent-keys) instead of OAuth, set `bearer_token_env_var` to the name of an environment variable that holds your agent API key. In this example, `AGENT_API_KEY` is a placeholder; replace it with the actual name of your environment variable, not the name of the variable wrapped in braces.
L100: ```toml
L101: [mcp_servers.stripe]
L102: url = "https://mcp.stripe.com"
L103: bearer_token_env_var = "AGENT_API_KEY" # Replace with the name of your environment variable
L104: ```
L105: #### ChatGPT
L106: 
L107: You can [install the official Stripe plugin in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_connector_690ab09fa43c8191bca40280e4563238). Connect your Stripe account and grant permissions to ChatGPT in the OAuth window when prompted.

L172: Working with Devin
L173: # Devin MCP servers and marketplace
L174: 
L175: Connect Devin to external tools with MCP servers: install plugins from the marketplace or add custom STDIO, SSE, or HTTP servers.
L176: 
L177: Copy page Copy page
L178: 
L179: MCP is an open protocol that enables Devin to use hundreds of external tools and data sources. Devin supports 3 transport methods (stdio, SSE, and HTTP).
L180: ## Why use MCP?
L181: 
L182: With MCP, Devin can help you:
L183: 
L184:   * dig through Sentry, Datadog and Vercel logs
L185:   * 【124†use Devin as a data analyst†devin.ai】 in Slack with database MCPs
L186:   * dig into SonarQube, CircleCI, and Jam issues
L187:   * bulk create Linear tickets, Notion docs, Google Docs (through Zapier) and more
L188:   * pull in context from and interact with Airtable, Stripe, and Hubspot
L189:   * a lot more!
L190: ## Get started with MCPs
L191: MCP servers are managed on the 【125†Customize → MCPs†app.devin.ai】 tab, alongside plugins, skills, hooks, and rules, at the personal, organization, or enterprise scope.
L192: (The older Settings → Connections → MCP servers page redirects there.) The recommended way to add an integration is to install its plugin from the plugin marketplace (the Marketplace list on the Plugins tab of the Customize page): most marketplace plugins are a single MCP server, often with skills that teach Devin how to use it, and installing one at the organization scope makes it available to everyone. The legacy MCP marketplace is still available from the MCPs tab.
